body.statement:
Fix deterministic total orders on all encoded finite sets.  The certificate-compression question has the following affirmative answer, with an unavoidable complexity qualification.  The handle \(\mathsf{Handle}\) has a deterministic exact-rational realization which enumerates \(\mathcal P_k\), chooses the first minimizing panel \(S^\star\), sets \(v^\star=\overline W(S^\star)\), and constructs a finite least-undecided-candidate branch tree.  The independently executable map \(\mathsf{Check}\) accepts the resulting \(\mathsf{Cert}\), and its acceptance certifies
\[
v^\star=\overline W(S^\star)=D^\star.
\]
For every rational instance with \(|\mathcal X|=3\) and \(|\mathcal C|\leq5\), exact exhaustive panel enumeration, the generator, and \(\mathsf P_{\mathrm{MILP}}\) agree on the optimum and on the complete set of minimizing panels; a common deterministic tie rule returns the same panel.

Moreover, a certificate of polynomial encoding length is guaranteed by the computable structural condition
\[
\text{there is }S_0\in\mathcal P_k\text{ such that }
\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d_{\pi xc}:c\in S_0\}\bigr)
=
\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d_{\pi xc}:c\in\mathcal C\}\bigr)
\quad
\text{for every }(\pi,x)\in\mathcal F\times\mathcal X.                 \tag{SC}
\]
Under \(\mathrm{(SC)}\), the certificate tree has only its root.  A sufficient condition is obtained by choosing, for each \((\pi,x)\) whose full-library minimum is below the dummy cost \(1\), the first candidate attaining that minimum and taking their union \(H\): if \(|H|\leq k\), then \(H\) satisfies \(\mathrm{(SC)}\).  This sufficient condition takes \(O(|\mathcal F||\mathcal X||\mathcal C|)\) exact rational comparisons to check.  No polynomial-time exact generator is asserted on unrestricted instances; such a generator would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
body.proof_tex:
Define, for each \(S\subseteq\mathcal C\),
\[
g(S)=\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_x
\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d_{\pi xc}:c\in S\}\bigr).                       \tag{1}
\]
The established exact-rational generator and core-compression theorem gives, using the sharp-width identity,
\[
g(S)=\overline W(S)                                                       \tag{2}
\]
for every panel \(S\), and constructs the first minimizer \(S^\star\in\mathcal P_k\) with
\[
v^\star=g(S^\star)=\min_{S\in\mathcal P_k}g(S)=D^\star.               \tag{3}
\]
Its deterministic tree construction closes a node \((I,E,O)\) precisely when
\[
|I|>k
\quad\text{or}\quad
g(I\cup E)\geq v^\star,                                                  \tag{4}
\]
and otherwise branches on the least element of \(E\).  The same theorem proves that \(|E|\) decreases at each edge, so the tree is finite, and that all structural and rational tests performed independently by \(\mathsf{Check}\) succeed.  Applying the established certificate soundness conclusion within that theorem to (2)--(4) yields
\[
\mathsf{Check}(\mathsf{Cert})=\mathrm{true}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
v^\star=\overline W(S^\star)=D^\star.                                  \tag{5}
\]
This proves the generator-and-checker part of the claim without treating a floating-point solver status as evidence.

For \(|\mathcal C|\leq5\), the number of feasible panels is bounded by
\[
|\mathcal P_k|=\sum_{j=0}^{k}{|\mathcal C|\choose j}\leq2^5=32.        \tag{6}
\]
The established theorem evaluates every panel by the same exact rational expression (1).  It also invokes the mixed-integer equivalence for every integral selection vector, under which the minimized assignment-variable objective is exactly \(g(S)\).  Therefore exact enumeration, the generator, and the mixed-integer formulation agree panel by panel, hence on both the optimum and its full argmin set.  This argument is valid for every three-cell rational instance with at most five candidates; the three-cell restriction is the requested bounded audit, not a condition needed for the equality.  A shared total order resolves ties identically.

It remains to verify that the displayed structural condition gives genuine compression.  Under \(\mathrm{(SC)}\), multiply each coordinatewise equality by the positive weight \(q_x\), sum over \(x\), and maximize over \(\pi\).  By (1),
\[
g(S_0)=g(\mathcal C).                                                     \tag{7}
\]
For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal C\), enlarging the set over which a minimum is taken cannot increase that minimum.  Hence
\[
g(S)\geq g(\mathcal C).                                                   \tag{8}
\]
Because \(S_0\in\mathcal P_k\), equations (3), (7), and (8) imply
\[
g(\mathcal C)\leq v^\star\leq g(S_0)=g(\mathcal C),
\qquad  ext{so}\qquad
v^\star=g(\mathcal C).                                                    \tag{9}
\]
At the root, \(I\cup E=\mathcal C\), so (9) satisfies the second leaf test in (4) with equality.  The tree therefore consists of that single root.  The established theorem also proves that the root label, the incumbent characteristic vector, and the exactly evaluated rational value have encoding length polynomial in the rational input length.

For the advertised sufficient test, let
\[
\delta_{\pi x}=
\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d_{\pi xc}:c\in\mathcal C\}\bigr).             \tag{10}
\]
Whenever \(\delta_{\pi x}<1\), finiteness of \(\mathcal C\) gives an attaining candidate; put the first such candidate into \(H\).  If \(\delta_{\pi x}<1\), this candidate gives a minimum over \(H\) no larger than \(\delta_{\pi x}\), while \(H\subseteq\mathcal C\) gives the reverse inequality.  If \(\delta_{\pi x}=1\), the dummy cost makes both minima equal to \(1\).  Thus
\[
\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d_{\pi xc}:c\in H\}\bigr)=\delta_{\pi x}
\quad  ext{for every }(\pi,x).                                           \tag{11}
\]
Consequently \(|H|\leq k\) implies \(H\in\mathcal P_k\) and proves \(\mathrm{(SC)}\) with \(S_0=H\).  Computing (10), the tie-broken minimizers, and their union uses \(O(|\mathcal F||\mathcal X||\mathcal C|)\) exact comparisons.

Finally, the established theorem combines this construction with the frozen NP-hardness result: an unrestricted polynomial-time generator would return the exact value \(D^\star\) in polynomial time, contradicting NP-hardness unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).  This proves the stated complexity qualification and completes every clause of the resolution.
